| `src/verification/families/b3_doe_inline.py` | B3-DOE-INLINE and B4-DOE-INLINE (M2.12): the system-ladder rung where the diffractive interaction's RAY OUTPUT is load-bearing, because a downstream refractive trace consumes it directly. None of them can gate, and the schema refuses the promotion rather than relying on the label. | The characterization layer; B4 never joins a required gate. |
| `src/verification/families/projection.py` | Projects registered families into claim_ledger Claims, so the coverage ledger is derived rather than typed twice. | Unchanged; the projection grows as families land. |
| `src/verification/__init__.py` | Package marker. | Unchanged. |

## Bucket B — candidate canonical case

| artifact | justification | destination in the new architecture |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `benchmarks/instances/b0_contract.py` | POSITIVE: the ten canonical B0 instances, executed. This is the only place each of the five negative outcomes -- unsupported, invalid_configuration, out_of_validity, lossy_but_allowed, blocked -- is produced by a DIFFERENT shipping component refusing a real request, and the only place the two ok-contract-wrong-physics traps are re-measured on the pinned installs rather than read out of a record. Freezing it keeps the five statuses individually reachable rather than individually declared. **Three instances are graphs through GraphExecutor; the other seven are refused before a graph could run -- a capability intersection, a bridge policy, an artifact-level declaration -- and go through the shipping refusal path, which is what those questions are about.** | B0-CONTRACT / B0-DTYPE / B0-VALIDITY / B0-UNITS canonical instances, run by tests/test_b0_instances.py in the default gate. |
| `benchmarks/instances/b1_ray.py` | POSITIVE: the five B1 ray families executed against the shipping Optiland adapter, and the only place three load-bearing conventions of the traced record are written down executably -- that a collimated on-axis ray's transverse position at the first surface IS its launch position (which makes sin(i) = rho/R exact), that the image plane refracts, and that a traced focal length is not a paraxial one. Each of those had a wrong reading that produced a plausible number, and each is now a comment beside the code that depends on it. **Also carries the device/precision matrix (RAY-4) and the unsupported-request probe (RAY-5). B1-RAY-LAGRANGE's gate was NOT_MET at 1.3e-7 against 1e-10 and is now MET at 1.2e-15 against 1e-13, because the ORACLE was corrected rather than the tolerance widened: the finite-real-ray bilinear form is preserved only by a LINEAR symplectic map, so the gate is now the DIFFERENTIAL invariant on two independent tangent vectors, extrapolated to zero ray separation. The 1.3e-7 finite-ray number is retained as a non-gating characterization metric at its original 1e-10 threshold. The device/precision matrix's CPU-vs-CUDA agreement is measured on real hardware and persisted at benchmarks/probes/records/optiland/b1_ray_device_precision.json.** | B1-RAY-EFL / -PLATE / -SNELL / -LAGRANGE / -OFFAXIS-OPL canonical instances, run by tests/test_b1_ray_instances.py in the default gate. |
| `benchmarks/instances/b1_wave.py` | POSITIVE: the seven B1 wave families executed through the Chromatix graph node, and the only place three families were found unable to support their own claims -- GAUSS/TILT/FWDBWD sitting outside their own sampling predicate while meeting their gates, TALBOT unable to revive because a binary grating's high orders dephase, and ASM-VALIDITY unable to demonstrate aliasing because an 8 um beam's bandwidth is fifty times inside the grid's. Each diagnosis is a comment beside the parameter it changed, and no tolerance moved. **Also carries the device observation (WAVE-3), whose CUDA arm is measured on real hardware and persisted at benchmarks/probes/records/chromatix/b1_wave_device_observation.json: the placement is read from array_state on the live JAX array before jax.device_get, and the persisted .npy placement is recorded beside it as a contrast because host bytes report cpu for every run. Asserted by tests/test_b1_wave_gpu.py. The complex64 accuracy cost (WAVE-2) is measured once, by B0-DTYPE-01, against the independent float64 angular spectrum rather than twice. TALBOT's tolerance basis is the m^4 non-paraxial order dephasing (pi/2) m^4 (lambda/d)^2, and the driver decomposes it against a paraxial and an exact float64 kernel on the same grid rather than asserting it.** | B1-WAVE-GAUSS / -AIRY / -TILT / -PLANEPHASE / -FWDBWD / -TALBOT / -ASM-VALIDITY canonical instances, run by tests/test_b1_wave_instances.py. |
| `benchmarks/instances/b1_gsl_validity.py` | POSITIVE: the 12 B1-GSL-VALIDITY instances executed against the shipping GENERALIZED_SNELL coupler, the smooth-limit agreement (float64 round-off over 9-45 samples/period) and the demonstrated period-axis and duty-cycle breakdowns this family exists to find. Also the place a genuine, pre-existing limitation of single_order_dominance's off-axis target direction and a non-monotonic reading of the coupler's own local-gradient-smoothness margin past its first refusal point were found and are recorded rather than silently worked around. **The three DUTY instances and PERIOD-06 refuse at the per-ray level (MISSING_DECLARATION) by design -- a genuinely discontinuous edge breaks the coupler's local-gradient estimate regardless of duty cycle -- and single_order_dominance is measured directly, bypassing that gate, so the family still records a graded signal on those instances.** | B1-GSL-VALIDITY-PERIOD-{01..08}, -DUTY-{01..03} and -OFFAXIS-01 canonical instances. |
| `benchmarks/instances/b2_transitions.py` | POSITIVE: the four B2 transition families executed -- exact ray-to-wave, the route budget on two systems, the stochastic wave-to-ray estimator with its four evidence kinds in enforced order, and the round trip in both directions with both arms. Four constructions had to be corrected to get here and every one of them had already produced a plausible number: the reconstruction was owed the SI eq S5 1/N, enumerating a MAGNITUDE density is not the exactness limit, unbiasedness must be measured on a SIGNED linear functional against an independent probe rather than on a norm or against the field itself, and a centred real Gaussian probe cannot see either broken twin. No tolerance moved; two tolerance BASES were completed. **The three W2R blind spots are measured rather than asserted, and two of the six controls needed their own configuration to be observable at all -- normal_sign is exactly inert at z = 0 and the evanescent fraction is exactly 0 at that pitch, so both would have reported green.** | B2-R2W-EXACT-01, B2-R2W-ROUTE-{ONNODE,OFFNODE}-{01,02,04,08}, B2-W2R-STOCH-01 and the B2-ROUNDTRIP canonical instances, run by tests/test_b2_transition_instances.py. |
| `benchmarks/instances/b2_equiv.py` | POSITIVE: the patch/global equivalence anchor, the drawn convergence ladder, and the enumerated sub-aperture instance that separates "the estimator is wrong" from "the estimator has sampling error". It also records the family's most useful finding: the equivalence is exact where the patch mode grid and the oracle mode grid coincide and only there -- 1.7e-15 at the DOE plane against 0.84 at z = 1.26 mm, with neither route wrong. **Two of the three negative controls are exactly inert at full aperture -- coverage is 1 and the launch offset is 0 -- which is how a real A_patch/A_draw inversion survived. The anchor measures that blindness as a number and the sub-aperture instances gate the controls.** | B2-EQUIV-FULL-01, B2-EQUIV-SUB-{004,016,064,225} and B2-EQUIV-SUB-ENUMERATED, run by tests/test_b2_equiv_instances.py. |
| `benchmarks/instances/b3_psf_singlet.py` | POSITIVE: this is the substrate proof. It is the only place a real Optiland trace becomes a real ExecutionRecord and that record is handed to verify() against a real family, so freezing it keeps the loop -- family, instance, executor, verifier -- exercised end to end by the test suite rather than by a person remembering to run it. **CHE-115 closed this. It reproduces the frozen fft_oracle_intensity_relative_l2 = 0.0022072391812867093 BIT-IDENTICALLY from the committed graph document examples/graphs/psf_singlet_sensor.yaml -- asserted with ==, not approx, by tests/test_substrate_proof.py::test_the_frozen_number_is_reproduced_bit_identically. The two things that had to change were config['advance_to_z_m'] on the C_RAY_TO_WAVE edge, without which a graph could not name the sensor plane at all, and reading the PSF with PsfNormalization.RAW rather than PEAK, because the metric peak-normalizes its own inputs and dividing twice costs one ULP.** | B3-PSF-SINGLET-01, the canonical instance, and the replacement for benchmarks/physics/L2-PSF-01/run_benchmark.py (CHE-115). |
| `benchmarks/systems/b3_4f_ideal.py` | POSITIVE: the ideal 4f relay driver -- fft2/mask/ifft2 realized directly with numpy, since no M_WAVE_CHROMATIX capability implements an ideal lens's Fourier-transforming property. Runs, measures and verifies all nine canonical instances and demonstrates every declared negative control firing on at least one of them. **Confirmed the order-n sign convention (x0_n = -n / Lf) and the finite-samples_per_period aliasing tail against scipy.special.jv while authoring; both are recorded in the family module's docstring rather than only in this driver.** | The nine B3-4F-IDEAL-* canonical instances. |
| `benchmarks/systems/b3_doe_inline.py` | POSITIVE: the embedded-DOE driver -- a diffractive interaction INSIDE a refractive train, so its outgoing ray bundle is handed straight to an Optiland trace with no reconstruction in between. Two topologies: collimated bundle into a linear phase ramp in front of a real singlet, and a converging bundle out of one singlet through the ramp into a second that relays the intermediate image at -1.914x. It computes its own reference rather than importing one -- closed_form_outgoing rebuilds the outgoing bundle from the grating equation and m phi(x_snap) / k0 and shares no line with couplers/generalized_snell.py, which a test enforces at the source level -- and runs six arms per instance so the exactness limits, the unmodulated Strehl denominator and the independently constructed admissible bundle are all measured rather than assumed. Its m = -1 instance is what found the order/OPL inconsistency in couplers/generalized_snell.py that CHE-148 fixed. | The twelve B3-DOE-INLINE-* and six B4-DOE-INLINE-* canonical instances. |
| `benchmarks/systems/b3_4f_real.py` | POSITIVE: the real aberrated 4f relay driver, and the first thing in this tree that composes the whole hybrid chain end to end -- C_WAVE_TO_RAY at full enumeration, an Optiland trace through a real refractive group, diffractive_interaction(model=FULL_FIELD) at the shared focal plane, a second Optiland trace, and a C_RAY_TO_WAVE sensor reconstruction. It imports B3-4F-IDEAL's own mask constructor and order reductions rather than copying them, which is what makes "the modulation is unchanged from 4F-1" true by identity. Drives both families and demonstrates all five declared negative controls firing. **Three things were found by running it rather than by deriving them, and each is recorded where a reader will meet it: displacing the ray LAUNCH POSITIONS does not displace the object (the spectral sum is periodic with the object grid, so the object grid is the field of view); the shared plane's axial position is not load-bearing at any displacement this geometry admits, because the field there is the object's own spectrum and its depth of focus is of order a metre; and the aperture axis has a hard ceiling where the aberration's residual ray angle stops fitting the shared plane's grid, which C_RAY_TO_WAVE refuses with SHAPE_MISMATCH.** | The five B3-4F-REAL-* and eight B4-4F-REAL-* canonical instances. |
| `benchmarks/systems/records/*.json` | POSITIVE: the nine B3-4F-IDEAL-* instance records -- the sweep across samples_per_period from deep inside to far outside the declared FFT_GRID_NYQUIST bound, plus the grid-snapped/off-grid carrier pair. | B3-4F-IDEAL-{SIN-01..05,BIN-01,BIN-02,CARRIER-SNAPPED,CARRIER-OFFGRID}. |
| `benchmarks/probes/ray_wave/demo2_hologram.py` | POSITIVE: demo2 is the composed ray-wave case that DOES have an independent decider -- the full-aperture patch validated against an independent float64 ASM at 7.1e-13 -- so freezing it gives B3 a second decidable composed instance beside the singlet, on a different coupler route. | B3-DEMO2-01 canonical instance. |
| `benchmarks/probes/ray_wave/demo3_hologram_lens.py` | POSITIVE: the paper's Fig 5c system is the repository's only case at a scale where the composition has no reference of its own, which is exactly what a characterization family must be anchored to. Freezing it keeps B4-DEMO3's cost and variance numbers comparable across the optimization work (CHE-118/119/120) rather than drifting with the configuration. | B4-DEMO3 canonical instance -- characterization only, validation_target false, no gating tolerance. |

## Families by layer — CHE-141 (M2.5)

Generated from `src/verification/families/`, not from `benchmarks/inventory.yaml`. The B0-B4 category says what may *decide* a family; the layer says what is being *claimed*, and the two are independent — `B3-PSF-SINGLET` and `B3-DUALROUTE` share a category, and one is a statement about an optical system while the other compares two numerical realizations of it.

Layer-C artifacts authored from M2.7 onward live in `benchmarks/systems/`. Existing layer-C evidence is **re-homed by classification, not moved on disk** — see `benchmarks/systems/README.md` for why, and `docs/benchmark_design.md` for the axis and its three consistency rules.

The instance counts below are the instances declared **on the family object**. B3 and B4 families construct theirs in their `benchmarks/instances/` drivers instead, so a zero there is a fact about where the instances are built and not an absence of evidence — `benchmarks/instances/records/` is the committed record set.

### Layer A — qualification

is this operator the thing it claims to be? Conventions, invariants, estimator exactness. Every family here owes a negative control. 20 families, 50 canonical instances declared on the family.

| family | category | components | what it claims |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `B0-CONTRACT` | B0 | `M_RAY_OPTILAND`, `M_WAVE_CHROMATIX`, `C_RAY_TO_WAVE`, `C_PATCH_WFT` | when a component is asked for something it cannot do, does it refuse with a code, a reason and a remedy -- and does the refusal say WHICH of the five negative outcomes it is? |
| `B0-DTYPE` | B0 | `M_WAVE_CHROMATIX` | when a precision request cannot be honoured, is the loss refused, or recorded as a MEASURED NUMBER -- and never performed silently? |
| `B0-UNITS` | B0 | `M_RAY_OPTILAND`, `M_WAVE_CHROMATIX` | can the substrate tell 'it executed' from 'it is right'? Both instances run perfectly, every boundary check passes, the contract status is ok, and the physics is wrong. |
| `B0-VALIDITY` | B0 | `C_PATCH_WFT` | when an instance crosses a declared validity bound, is that reported as OUT OF VALIDITY -- distinct from unsupported and from a malformed request? |
| `B1-RAY-EFL` | B1 | `M_RAY_OPTILAND` | does a traced thick plano-convex singlet in air reproduce the paraxial closed forms R/(n-1) for the effective focal length and EFL - t/n for the back focal length from the rear vertex? |
| `B1-RAY-LAGRANGE` | B1 | `M_RAY_OPTILAND` | is the differential optical invariant omega(v_a, v_b) = sum_k (dp_k^a dq_k^b - dp_k^b dq_k^a) -- with q the transverse position on a plane of constant z and p = n (L, M) the index-weighted direction cosines -- conserved by the real ray map through a multi-element system? Equivalently: is the traced map symplectic? |
| `B1-RAY-OFFAXIS-OPL` | B1 | `M_RAY_OPTILAND` | does the pupil OPL declared from an Optiland trace carry the full convergence tilt an off-axis field requires, including the object-space term n_object * (d0 . r_launch)? |
| `B1-RAY-PLATE` | B1 | `M_RAY_OPTILAND` | does a plane-parallel plate in a converging beam move the focus by t(1 - 1/n), AWAY from the plate? |
| `B1-RAY-SNELL` | B1 | `M_RAY_OPTILAND` | does refraction at a single planar interface satisfy n1 sin(theta1) = n2 sin(theta2) across the incidence range, and is total internal reflection reported as a validity boundary rather than as a numerical failure? |
| `B1-WAVE-AIRY` | B1 | `M_WAVE_CHROMATIX` | does the first dark ring of a focused circular aperture land at 0.61 lambda / NA? |
| `B1-WAVE-ASM-VALIDITY` | B1 | `M_WAVE_CHROMATIX` | where does the angular-spectrum method stop being trustworthy on this grid, and does crossing that boundary produce a plausible-looking wrong field rather than an exception? |
| `B1-WAVE-FWDBWD` | B1 | `M_WAVE_CHROMATIX` | does propagating a field forward by z and then backward by z return the input to the dtype's round-off floor? |
| `B1-WAVE-GAUSS` | B1 | `M_WAVE_CHROMATIX` | does a propagated Gaussian beam's 1/e^2 intensity radius follow w(z) = w0 sqrt(1 + (z/zR)^2)? |
| `B1-WAVE-PLANEPHASE` | B1 | `M_WAVE_CHROMATIX` | does propagating a plane wave a distance z advance its phase by exactly k_z z, with the sign the repository's phasor convention declares? |
| `B1-WAVE-TALBOT` | B1 | `M_WAVE_CHROMATIX` | does a periodic field revive itself at the Talbot distance z_T = 2 d^2 / lambda? |
| `B1-WAVE-TILT` | B1 | `M_WAVE_CHROMATIX` | does a tilted collimated beam walk off by z tan(theta), with the right SIGN, under a kykx-parameterized propagation? |
| `B2-EQUIV` | B2 | `C_PATCH_WFT`, `C_PLANAR_DOE_STEP` | does decomposing an aperture into patches and reassembling it give the same field as treating it globally, and how does the answer depend on patch granularity? |
| `B2-R2W-EXACT` | B2 | `C_RAY_TO_WAVE` | in the enumeration limit -- every term the estimator would sample, visited -- does C_RAY_TO_WAVE reduce to the reference field exactly? |
| `B2-ROUNDTRIP` | B2 | `C_RAY_TO_WAVE`, `C_WAVE_TO_RAY` | what survives a round trip through two representations, and -- the part that gives the answer meaning -- does the deliberately broken twin fail? |
| `B2-W2R-STOCH` | B2 | `C_WAVE_TO_RAY` | is the wave-to-ray estimator exact in the enumeration limit, unbiased, converging at the expected rate, and at a variance the required ray count can reach? Four questions, and they fail independently. |

### Layer B — numerical realization and validity

does a choice that should not move the answer stay inside its budget, and where does it stop? Every family here owes a refinement dimension. 5 families, 20 canonical instances declared on the family.

| family | category | components | what it claims |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `B1-GSL-VALIDITY` | B1 | `C_GENERALIZED_SNELL`, `C_PLANAR_DOE_STEP` | over what range of grating period (relative to wavelength and sample pitch), phase discontinuity and incidence angle does GENERALIZED_SNELL's per-ray local grating equation stay close to the analytic grating angle, and do its own declared validity margins predict the boundary? |
| `B2-R2W-ROUTE` | B2 | `C_RAY_TO_WAVE` | how much does the reconstruction route -- a parameter that should not change the answer -- actually change it, and at what cost? |
| `B3-DUALROUTE` | B3 | `C_RAY_TO_WAVE`, `M_RAY_OPTILAND` | on the Cooke triplet, do the ray-only and ray->coupler->wave PSF routes each conserve the traced bundle's power end to end? |
| `B4-COST` | B4 | `M_RAY_OPTILAND`, `M_WAVE_CHROMATIX`, `C_RAY_TO_WAVE`, `C_PATCH_WFT` | what does each node and each route cost, and how much of a run is framework overhead rather than physics? |
| `B4-DUALROUTE-AGREEMENT` | B4 | `M_RAY_OPTILAND`, `C_RAY_TO_WAVE` | how far apart are the three PSF routes on the Cooke triplet, and what accounts for the gap? NOT: which of them is right -- all three are our own code. |

### Layer C — system

is a physically meaningful end-to-end optical system modelled correctly? Every family here owes a topology and two observables. 8 families, 0 canonical instances declared on the family.

| family | category | components | what it claims |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `B3-4F-IDEAL` | B3 | `M_WAVE_CHROMATIX` | **topology:** input field → ideal Fourier transform → Fourier-plane modulation → ideal inverse Fourier transform → image field<br>**observables:** order_location_error_frac, order_phase_error_rad, order_power_relative_l2, total_power_relative_error |
| `B3-4F-REAL` | B3 | `M_RAY_OPTILAND`, `C_WAVE_TO_RAY`, `C_PLANAR_DOE_STEP`, `C_RAY_TO_WAVE` | **topology:** object field → C_WAVE_TO_RAY (full enumeration of the object's angular spectrum) → ray propagation through a real refractive group (M_RAY_OPTILAND) → DiffractiveInteraction, model=full_field, at the shared focal plane → ray propagation through a real refractive group (M_RAY_OPTILAND) → C_RAY_TO_WAVE coherent sensor reconstruction<br>**observables:** clipped_power_fraction, field_phase_rms_vs_ideal_rad, field_relative_l2_vs_ideal_4f, fourier_plane_power_relative_error, order_location_error_frac, order_phase_error_rad, order_power_relative_l2, psf_centroid_shift_px, psf_fwhm_relative_error |
| `B3-DEMO2` | B3 | `C_RAY_TO_WAVE`, `C_PATCH_WFT` | **topology:** coherent plane-wave illumination → C_PATCH_WFT → free-space ray propagation to the sensor plane → C_RAY_TO_WAVE → sensor-plane intensity<br>**observables:** demo2_ncc, demo2_relative_l2, patch_handoff_power_ratio |
| `B3-DOE-INLINE` | B3 | `M_RAY_OPTILAND`, `C_GENERALIZED_SNELL`, `C_RAY_TO_WAVE` | **topology:** collimated (or tilted) coherent ray bundle, or a converging bundle from a real refractive group → DiffractiveInteraction, model=generalized_snell, at a planar linear-ramp surface → outgoing ray bundle, handed DIRECTLY to a refractive trace → ray propagation through real refractive optics (M_RAY_OPTILAND) → C_RAY_TO_WAVE coherent reconstruction at the image plane<br>**observables:** admissible_bundle_field_residual, downstream_clipped_power_fraction, grating_equation_direction_residual, interaction_power_ratio_error, order_position_field_relative_error, order_position_relative_error, order_position_vs_admissible_residual_m, outgoing_amplitude_residual, outgoing_opl_rebase_residual_waves, psf_fwhm_relative_error, refractive_limit_residual_waves, strehl_quantization_relative_error |
| `B3-PSF-SINGLET` | B3 | `C_RAY_TO_WAVE` | **topology:** M_RAY_OPTILAND → C_RAY_TO_WAVE → M_WAVE_CHROMATIX → sensor-plane intensity<br>**observables:** fft_oracle_intensity_relative_l2, handoff_power_ratio, o2_asm_intensity_relative_l2, reconstructed_power_ray_doubling_excess |
| `B4-4F-REAL` | B4 | `M_RAY_OPTILAND`, `C_WAVE_TO_RAY`, `C_PLANAR_DOE_STEP`, `C_RAY_TO_WAVE` | **topology:** object field → C_WAVE_TO_RAY (full enumeration of the object's angular spectrum) → ray propagation through a real refractive group (M_RAY_OPTILAND) → DiffractiveInteraction, model=full_field, at the shared focal plane → ray propagation through a real refractive group (M_RAY_OPTILAND) → C_RAY_TO_WAVE coherent sensor reconstruction<br>**observables:** clipped_power_fraction, field_phase_rms_vs_ideal_rad, field_relative_l2_vs_ideal_4f, fourier_plane_power_relative_error, order_location_error_frac, order_phase_error_rad, order_power_relative_l2, psf_centroid_shift_px, psf_fwhm_relative_error |
| `B4-DEMO3` | B4 | `C_PATCH_WFT`, `C_RAY_TO_WAVE` | **topology:** coherent plane-wave illumination → C_PATCH_WFT → M_RAY_OPTILAND → C_RAY_TO_WAVE → sensor-plane intensity<br>**observables:** ncc_vs_ray_count_slope, route_agreement_ncc, seed_to_seed_ncc, stage_power_ratio |
| `B4-DOE-INLINE` | B4 | `M_RAY_OPTILAND`, `C_GENERALIZED_SNELL`, `C_RAY_TO_WAVE` | **topology:** collimated (or tilted) coherent ray bundle, or a converging bundle from a real refractive group → DiffractiveInteraction, model=generalized_snell, at a planar linear-ramp surface → outgoing ray bundle, handed DIRECTLY to a refractive trace → ray propagation through real refractive optics (M_RAY_OPTILAND) → C_RAY_TO_WAVE coherent reconstruction at the image plane<br>**observables:** admissible_bundle_field_residual, coherent_vs_geometric_relative_l2, downstream_clipped_power_fraction, fringe_contrast_coherent, fringe_contrast_geometric, grating_equation_direction_residual, high_band_spectrum_fraction_coherent, high_band_spectrum_fraction_geometric, interaction_power_ratio_error, order_position_field_relative_error, order_position_relative_error, order_position_vs_admissible_residual_m, outgoing_amplitude_residual, outgoing_opl_rebase_residual_waves, psf_fwhm_relative_error, refractive_limit_residual_waves, strehl_quantization_relative_error |
